jurisdiction.name: Liberia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Liberia has no AI law, AI strategy or regulator guidance on AI. Its only official AI-related policy text is the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' Whole of Government National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, which plans AI chatbots in public services and commits to a national AI strategy by early 2027. A data protection bill is still pending and there is no data protection authority.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The planned national AI strategy and the pending data protection bill are listed as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Liberia; commissioned by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications
instruments.current_status: Published on the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications' Policies & Regulations page. The document is undated; the year 2025 is taken from its own text (validation workshop 11 December 2024, stakeholder inputs through January 2025, strategy period 2025-2029). It records that no national AI strategy, policy or regulation exists yet and sets a target of developing and approving an AI strategy by Q1 2027 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Liberia's whole-of-government digital strategy for 2025-2029, built on three pillars (Digital Infrastructure & Cyber Security; Governance & Services; Digital Empowerment of Citizens and Businesses) with costed initiatives, an implementation roadmap and an M&E framework. Its only AI-specific content is under government process digitization: it plans AI-powered chatbots for routine public-service inquiries (targets: an AI strategy developed and approved by Q1 2027, AI bots handling 50% of routine inquiries by Q4 2028 and 70% of tickets resolved by AI chatbots by Q2 2029). It also proposes a National ICT Governing Board, a Liberia Digital Transformation Agency and a CIO Council to govern implementation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National digital strategy with a small AI element (public-sector AI chatbots) and an explicit commitment to develop a national AI strategy by Q1 2027; the main official AI-related policy document found for Liberia.
metadata_gaps: publication_date: the document states no issue date; year 2025 derived from the document's own consultation timeline and strategy period

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Liberia were searched, including the posts and telecommunications ministry's laws and policies, the legislature, ministries and regulators. Only the Whole of Government National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 was recorded; no AI law, national AI strategy or other qualifying material was found, and a data protection bill is pending. Not yet verified from the official text: the legislature's bill tracker and the ministry's Strategic Plan 2025-2029, which was unavailable.

leads.title: National AI strategy (planned)

No draft found on official sites as of 2026-10-12.

leads.title: An Act for the Collection, Processing, Transmission, Storage, Protection, and Use of Personal Information in Liberia (Data Protection Bill)
leads.issuing_authority: President of Liberia / House of Representatives
leads.note: Pending bill. The Digital Strategy (2025-2029) states the Data Protection Law had been validated by stakeholders pending submission to the Legislature; press reports say the President submitted it and the House referred it to its Committee on Posts and Telecommunications. No official text or enactment found on official sites; record under data-privacy once enacted and published. Deep sweep 2026-11-08: no change. News of 11 June 2025 (smartnewsliberia.com, discovery only): the President submitted the bill and it was referred to the House Committee on Post and Telecommunications. No evidence of passage found in November 2026 searches.

leads.title: National ICT Policy (2025-2029/2030)
leads.note: The Digital Strategy says a new national ICT policy has been drafted and is under consultation; not found on mopt.gov.lr (only the 2019-2024 policy, which has no AI content, is posted). Check for AI content once published. Deep sweep 2026-11-08: the draft is now on mopt.gov.lr (file name 'Draft 1 Jan 7 2025'; no printed date or draft marking; contains placeholders such as 'To be written upon completion of this document'). AI appears only in passing: Pillar 2 'Design and deploy AI-enabled learning solutions' with a target of an AI in Education Platform piloted by 2026 and scaled by 2028; s.3.1.4 Objective 7 'Develop a National AI Policy'; grants for AI projects. No AI regulation, ethics or AI body. Fails the scope test as a draft general ICT policy; re-check the adopted version.

leads.title: MOPT Strategic Plan 2025-2029 'Digital Liberia: Equity, Sovereignty and Innovation for a Connected Future'

leads.note: Indexed at https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/MOPT-Strategic-Plan-2025-2029-final.pdf but the URL returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-12 and the file is not in the ministry's media library; reportedly includes an ICT-driven innovation priority. Check for AI content if re-posted. 2026-11-01: the PDF now loads; cover reads 2025-2029 with no other printed date. AI appears only in passing (AI and innovation hubs, an AI-enabled monitoring dashboard, a need to regulate AI); stays a lead.

leads.title: Draft National Data Governance Policy
leads.english_title: Liberia Draft National Data Governance Policy (2026)
leads.note: Draft on the ministry's site, cover dated 2026 and marked DRAFT; the text says it will be published once approved. Section 7.2 requires government agencies using AI to run privacy, ethics and non-discrimination impact assessments and makes all AI systems auditable and subject to oversight by the Independent Information Commission; sections 9.2(c) and (e) cover bias and transparency in automated decisions. AI is a section of a general data policy; record once approved if the AI provisions remain.

leads.title: Cybercrime Act of 2025
leads.note: News only (allafrica.com, 16 January 2026, discovery): Senate concurrence notified to the House around 15 January 2026; awaiting presidential assent. Reported offences: unauthorised access, digital fraud, identity theft, online harassment, illegal interception; no AI or deepfake provisions reported. The cybercrime text earlier posted by MoPT has no AI provisions. Check the enacted text (gazette or mopt.gov.lr) for deepfake or synthetic-media offences.
